.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes have been made to the forecast this morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and warmer today.

- 2) Showers and a few thunderstorms late tonight through 
  Thursday night.

- 3) Daily shower and thunderstorm chances continue this weekend
  and into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and warmer today.

High pressure over the Mid-Atlantic today and a southerly flow 
will allow for temperatures to be about 5 to 7 degrees above 
average this afternoon. Although we can't rule out a shower in 
spots between the Appalachian Front and the Shenandoah Valley 
this afternoon, most areas will remain dry. High temperatures 
may approach 90.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Showers and a few thunderstorms late tonight 
through Thursday night.

As the high breaks down and continues to slide to the east
tonight into early Thursday, a cold front will approach the 
region from the northwest. It will be relatively slow in 
movement to the south and east. A couple of showers or a rumble
of thunder could develop along the front and move into western
Maryland overnight tonight shortly after midnight and continue
to propagate southeastward throughout the night. Due to the lack
of daytime heating, the convection should be mainly due to low-
level moisture and gradual lift from an approaching cold front.
Some upper-level energy and a jet streak aloft could add 
additional lift to showers and a couple of thunderstorms across 
the region during the day Thursday and into Thursday night. 
However, a westerly component to the wind in the lower levels 
could act as a downsloping effect and squash some of this 
convection in a few places. Highs Thursday could reach the upper
80s to near 90 and dewpoint temperatures could reach the upper 
60s to low 70s. The front should be slow to move to the south 
and east that showers and thunderstorms could linger well into 
the night Thursday night. Showers and any thunderstorms should 
become more spotty or isolated Friday morning with the front 
nearly stalling across the Virginia Piedmont. Highs Friday 
should be a couple of degrees cooler due to cloud cover, 
convection and a northerly component to the wind on the north 
side of the front.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Daily shower and thunderstorm chances continue
this weekend and into early next week.

On Saturday, surface high pressure over New England shifts offshore 
as a cold front approaches from the northwest. Surface winds shift 
to southerly, ushering in a more humid airmass. With increased 
humidity, showers and thunderstorms are possible Saturday and Sunday 
although are expected to remain below severe criteria. 

Going into next week, precipitation chances linger but remain low 
(less than 20%). A low pressure system is currently forecast to 
track across the Great Lakes with the associated cold fronts 
impacting the Mid-Atlantic. Temperatures will be in the 70s and
80s each day with high humidity values yielding heat indices in
the low 90s for some.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected to prevail through the end of the
week. Shower and t-storm activity could bring brief 
restrictions on Thursday (mainly in the afternoon and/or 
evening). Winds remain S/SW through tonight (with some gusts up 
to 20 kt possible this afternoon) until a cold front brings a 
shift to W/NW Thursday morning. Some fog/low clouds are possible
Thursday night into Friday morning.

Low clouds are possible late Friday night. Winds remain out of 
the south Saturday and Sunday with daily precipitation chances 
bringing brief periods of sub-VFR conditions. Winds on Saturday 
gust 10 to 15 knots with winds remaining light on Sunday. Showers
are possible Saturday along with a possible afternoon thunderstorm.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds will increase this afternoon into tonight, when 
advisories will be in effect for all waters. Winds shift to the 
west and northwest and could remain gusty Thursday as a cold 
front crosses, possibly bringing a few showers and 
thunderstorms. Sub-SCA level north to northwesterly winds are 
most likely over the waters on Friday. 

Winds shift to southerly on Saturday with southerly channeling 
yielding Small Craft Advisory criteria winds in the afternoon. Winds 
diminish overnight and remain below SCA criteria on Sunday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tide levels will remain elevated (0.5 to 1 ft above normal)
through Thursday morning. Sensitive sites could approach minor 
flood at times, mainly late tonight into early Thursday 
morning, though west-of-south flow by this time lowers 
confidence. More notable water level decreases will occur 
Thursday behind a cold front.
